lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Figma has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide by about 5.5-6% in each of the last two quarters. Q1 2026 came in at $333.4M against a $315-317M guide (+5.5%), Q2 at $370.1M against $348-350M (+6.0%), and Q4 2025 at $303.8M was above its range. The Q3 guide of $373-375M implies only about 1% sequential growth, against 11% from Q1 to Q2. On the call the CFO called it a 'snapshot' that excludes beta products, which he labelled upside. Repeating the pattern would give about $390-397M, 3-5% above the about $377M consensus, which sits only about 1% above the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, a 5.5% beat over the guide midpoint plus a $55M FY raise, closed +13.24% (2026-05-14). Q2 2026, a 6.0% beat plus a $40M FY raise, closed -14.85% (2026-08-05) on AI cost of revenue (+117%) and the soft Q3 sequential guide. A revenue beat by itself has not set the sign on this name.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-25, partway through Q3, Figma gave 2x more AI credits on Professional and 1.6x on Organization/Enterprise add-ons at an unchanged price. The pay-as-you-go spending cap also stayed the same, so it now buys more usage. That is an effective per-credit price cut of about 50% and 37.5%. The CFO had said on 08-05 that most AI revenue comes through coterminous add-ons and warned a shift to pay-as-you-go would add variability. This lowers the AI-credit expansion and overage revenue per unit of usage for 5 weeks of Q3 and all of the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AI monetization has moved the stock before: March 2026 credit-limit enforcement drew a selloff on churn/monetization fears (https://rallies.ai/news/figma-tumbles-as-march-ai-credit-enforcement-revives-churn-and-monetization-concerns). No earnings print has yet isolated AI-credit revenue as a line.

findings.finding: The Figma agent in Design and Weave moved from open beta to general availability on 2026-10-06 and now consumes paid AI credits. The CFO said on 08-05 that beta and early-access products (agent, Make on local code, Motion and others) are excluded from guidance and would be upside once monetized. The Q4 guide given tonight is the first that can include a paid agent.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises were bought in May (+13.24%) and sold in August (-14.85%). In August the sequential Q3 guide was the line cited as a deceleration worry.

findings.finding: The guide already embeds deep H2 operating-margin compression. FY2026 non-GAAP operating income is guided at $125-135M and was maintained on 08-05. H1 delivered about $89M (Q1 about 16% of $333.4M, about $53M; Q2 $36.1M), so H2 is guided at about $41M on about $762M of revenue, roughly a 5% margin against about 13% in H1. A revenue beat at Figma's usual 85% gross margin clears that bar easily.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's -14.85% was attributed to profit reversal and AI cost (https://www.webull.com/news/15358948900545536). That is the line this name has traded on most recently, so a profit beat matters.

findings.finding: Q3 carried the full inference cost of the Figma agent and other beta features with no revenue, because the agent was free until GA on 10-06. The CFO said Figma 'bears the cost of inference' on beta and that gross margin 'will vary from quarter to quarter in the near term'. Q2 non-GAAP gross margin of 85% had risen 2.5 points q/q, so a Q3 step back is the risk on the line that sank the August print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: cost of revenue +117% and AI costs were cited for -14.85% (https://bingx.com/en/news/post/why-is-figma-fig-stock-price-down-today-august-rising-ai-costs-and-slower-growth-outlook-trigger-a-selloff).

findings.finding: The sell-side bar was cut in the three weeks before the print. Wells Fargo cut its target 34->30 (10-12), Stifel 25->22 Hold (10-14) and Citi 37->35 (10-28), and two new Hold/Neutral initiations came on 11-02 (Telsey; Redburn at $23, roughly spot). Consensus is 11 Hold of 16.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 prints analysts cut targets after a beat; the stock went +6.9% and +13.24% on those prints.

findings.finding: Short interest was 12.05% of float with 3.85 days to cover on 2026-10-15, down 9.2% from 13.3% on 09-30. The short is meaningful but not crowded, and was being covered into the print, against a +11.76-point put skew.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ahead of May 2026 the stock rose on 'heavy short positioning' and then gained +13.24% on the print (https://rallies.ai/news/figma-jumps-as-oversold-bounce-meets-heavy-short-positioning-before-may-14-earnings).

findings.finding: Expansion signals softened in Q2. Net dollar retention fell to 136% from 139% in Q1. The CFO said customers are hiring below original plans because of AI productivity, while about two-thirds of $10K+ customers still added seats at renewal. He also flagged tougher Q3/Q4 comps from lapping the March 2025 pricing change. A further NDR decline is the seat-compression read the AI-disruption bears want.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NDR rose to 139% with the +13.24% May print and fell to 136% with the -14.85% August print; on this name it has gone with the reaction both times.

findings.finding: Sezzle has beaten revenue consensus by about 11-12% in each recent quarter: Q3 2025 $116.8M vs $104.7M (+11.5%), Q2 2026 $149.7M vs about $133-135M (+11-12%). Q3 2026 consensus of about $154M (+32% y/y) sits exactly on management's 'around 30%' H2 growth guide, so a beat of mid-single digits or more on the reported quarter is the base case. But the stock fell -12.5% (Nov 2025) and -33.9% (Aug 2026) on the last two beats of that kind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats of about 11% came with -12.47% (2025-11-05, beat plus GMV slowdown and credit worries) and -33.89% (2026-08-06, beat plus a raise, sold on 'around 30%' H2 growth and yield normalising), and with +35.26% (2026-02-25) and +16.04% (2026-05-06) when the guide was raised sharply. The beat by itself has not set the sign.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management pre-warned three things for Q3: provisions could exceed 3% of GMV in Q3 (the FY framework is 2.5-3%; Q2 was 2.4%), revenue yield would decline sequentially as Pagaya and SezzleCash dilute the take rate, and marketing (Q2 $19.4M, 'not a run rate') would come down. A Q3 provision above 3% of GMV and a lower yield therefore land inside what the company guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit worries were cited in the -12.47% reaction of 2025-11-05; yield normalisation was the stated reason for the -33.89% reaction of 2026-08-06.

findings.finding: A first FY2027 outlook is likely at this print: with the Q3 2025 print on 2025-11-05 Sezzle issued its first FY2026 adjusted EPS guide ($4.35), which it then raised to $4.70, $5.10 and $5.25. So this release probably carries a new-year guide, and the street has no company anchor for 2027. The sign is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has set the sign on every real print. First FY2026 guide on 2025-11-05: -12.47%. Raises in Feb and May 2026: +35.26% and +16.04%. Raise with an H2 deceleration in Aug 2026: -33.89%.

findings.finding: SEZL rose about +13.4% on 2026-11-04 (122.43 to ~138.8) into the print, on a fintech sympathy move with Upstart +11% and Affirm +7%. Upstart's Q3 print (2026-11-03) had originations +44% y/y, but CEO Paul Gu said 'macro is putting pressure on our near-term outlook', and its FY guide implies Q4 revenue of about $307M against Q3's $371M. findings.finding: The reported quarter was pre-guided and the bar has come down. On 2026-08-06 the CFO said Q3 CELSIUS brand should 'look a lot like the second' (Q2: -11.7% y/y to about $387M) and gross margin should stay in the high 40s. Since then Chartmill shows the Q3 revenue estimate cut 7.57% in three months, and JPMorgan, UBS and TD Cowen cut targets. Bottom-up arithmetic (CELSIUS about -12% on Q3 2025's ~$393M, plus Alani Nu about +20% on $332.0M, plus Rockstar about $66M) gives roughly $810M, inside the $800-816M bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed $870-886M consensus by about 6% and the stock fell 18.46%. Q3 2025 beat revenue ($725.1M vs $715.7M) and EPS ($0.42 vs $0.27) and still fell 24.8% on the Q4 'noise' warning. This name has not paid for the reported quarter when the forward read is soft.

findings.finding: Alani Nu consumption ran ahead into Q3. Management said Alani scans were about +50% after the Witch's Brew launch (Barclays, 2026-09-08; Witch's Brew billed on Aug 6 as 'the largest limited-time offer in the brand's history'). PepsiCo's Q3 prepared remarks (2026-10-08, 12 weeks to Sept 5) say 'the partnership with Celsius Holdings gained value share and holds nearly 20 percent share of the category'. Q2 Alani reported net sales grew +21% against +56% scans. If the Q3 gross-to-net gap narrows now the Pepsi DSD transition is complete, Alani could print above the roughly +20% (about $400M) implied in the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: Alani +21% reported was not enough to offset CELSIUS -12%, and the stock fell 18.46%. Q1 2026 (+4.45%) and Q4 2025 (+6.94%) were Alani-led beats bought modestly. On this name Alani strength buys single digits; CELSIUS weakness costs double digits.

findings.finding: CELSIUS brand consumption got worse after the Q2 call. At Barclays on 2026-09-08 management put CELSIUS scans at -5% to -10% (IRI), against -2% tracked retail sales in Q2 that the CFO had called 'the consumer'. That undercuts the Aug 6 claim that the brand 'exit[s] the year back into growth', which matters for Q4/2027 commentary on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The forward read on CELSIUS drove the last two big moves: -24.8% on 2025-11-06 (Q4 noise warning) and -18.46% on 2026-08-06 (brand -12%, 'went too deep' on rationalization). The stock also fell 6.5% on 2026-09-09, the day after these scan figures.

findings.finding: Diesel rose well above the level the margin guide was set at. The Aug 6 high-40s gross margin guide was explicitly 'at current diesel and aluminum levels', with improvement only 'if fuel or aluminum moderates'. EIA on-highway diesel was $5.348 the week of Aug 3, $5.652 on Aug 24 and $5.967 on Sept 7 (+11.6% from the guide date), with secondary reports of a record about $6.53 the week of Sept 21. B. Riley's preview notes fuel costs rose in August and September. That pressures Q3 gross margin below Q2's 48.1% and the Q4 margin commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin compression was part of the Q2 miss (48.1% vs 51.5%, adjusted EBITDA -12%), and the stock fell 18.46%. Q3 2025 at 51.3% margin was overshadowed by the Q4 warning.

findings.finding: New forward information is promised for this call. On Aug 6 management said it would give more detail on 2027 innovation load-in timing 'after third-quarter results', and that a new 16-ounce CELSIUS offering launches 'in a meaningful way in '27'. The CFO at Barclays called the payoff 'a '27 and '28 play'. A first concrete 2027 calendar lands in this window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Forward commentary has moved this stock the most: -24.8% (Q4 noise, Nov 2025), +6.94% (Feb 2026, the 2026 setup), -18.46% (Aug 2026, Q3 'like Q2').

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 came after a 73% YTD run and fell 24.8% on a beat. Q2 2026 came off lows and still fell 18.46%. The last two prints with heavy expectations were sold.

findings.finding: The buyback is still running. The company repurchased $100.4M in Q2 ($124.5M in H1) and said it 'intend[s] to continue utilizing the $300 million authorization this year', which leaves up to about $175M for H2. Q3 traded at $24-29, so a large Q3 repurchase is likely to be reported.

findings.finding: New litigation in October 2026. Two proposed consumer class actions (W.D. Wash. and Illinois, filed around Oct 26-29) challenge the 'Burns Body Fat' and 'Accelerates Metabolism' front labels, and investor class action notices were issued on Nov 3. A prior labeling case settled for $7.8M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measurable prior print reaction to litigation.

findings.finding: The Q4 comparison is hard. Management flagged on Aug 6 that Q4 comparisons are affected by the prior-year inventory build tied to Alani Nu's Pepsi distribution transition, so the Q4 outlook on the call will likely show weak year-over-year optics. B. Riley instead argues Q4 compares favorably because Q4 2025 revenue fell 7.7% after Q3 2025's +44%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 commentary on the Q3 2025 call ('noise' from the Alani load-in) coincided with a 24.8% fall.

findings.finding: The distributor is under pressure in the period. PepsiCo said on 2026-10-08 that North America 'performed below our expectations', that PBNA organic revenue declined slightly on lower volume, and that structural cost reductions are coming. Celsius sells mostly through Pepsi's DSD system, so a cost-cutting distributor could keep CELSIUS inventory lean (the 'rebalancing' already seen) into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pepsi inventory reductions drove the Q3 2024 collapse ($100-120M destock) and the 2026 'rebalancing' gap: about half of Q2's 10-point gap between scans and net sales.

outside_window.finding: England plans to restrict sales of drinks above 150mg/L caffeine to under-16s, targeted for April 2027 and still needing parliamentary approval. Celsius is caught by the threshold; international was about 4.5% of Q1 sales.

A second North Carolina manufacturing line starts in H2 2026 with full benefit in 2027, and permanent CELSIUS innovation returns to shelves in 1H27. The margin and brand recovery are dated after the window; only the call's description of them is inside it (filed as a finding).
